name: Restfox
tagline: An HTTP client. Collections stay here. Requests leave when you send them.
description:
Build a collection of HTTP requests, press Send, and read the answer. Folders, query strings, headers, JSON or form bodies, Basic and Bearer auth, and environment variables — the same shape Restfox uses, kept on this device inside the app.

An unofficial port of Restfox by Flawid D'Souza (MIT). Collections never leave. A request leaves this browser the moment you send it, https only, up to 8 MB back.

SAME LIMIT AS RESTFOX IN A BROWSER. Some sites will refuse the call — that is the browser blocking a page from talking to another site, not this app being broken. Restfox's desktop app gets past that with its own proxy; this port does not. A checkbox can route through GifOS's public-host proxy, which only forwards to a curated list, not arbitrary addresses. Cookies are never attached. There are no live sockets, no plugins, and no file workspaces.

The app asks to reach any site, so GifOS labels it ⚠ Unsafe and you confirm the hosts before it can talk. Untick one and that host is gone.
